today.name: Nod by n8n
today.tagline: Open source personal agent with its own computer
today.description: Nod does the work around your work, in your apps and on real websites, using a private computer of its own on your Mac or PC. It takes orders only from you, asks before anything you didn't ask for, and runs on the AI provider you choose. Free, Apache 2.0.
today.category: Open Source • Artificial Intelligence • Virtual Assistants

today.name: Skillbox
today.tagline: One library for your AI skills, synced to every agent
today.description: Skillbox keeps your AI skills in one library and syncs them to Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. Follow GitHub sources, review diffs, and scan each version for prompt injection. Trim shortens noisy command output so sessions last longer.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, I'm Adenekan Wonderful, the maker of Skillbox.I built this because my AI skills were everywhere. A few lived in GitHub repos, some sat inside project folders, and some were installed for Claude Code but missing from Cursor. A better version of one would turn up and I'd have no idea. Copying files was easy. Knowing what I had, where it came from, whether it had changed, and whether it was safe was the hard part.So Skillbox does four things:One library, and a smaller active set. Keep everything you've collected, and deliver only what each tool or project needs. Every skill your agent loads costs context, so we don't treat "saved" as "installed".Sources stay attached. Skills added from GitHub or GitLab keep following their source. When one changes, you see the diff and decide whether to take it.Trust, per version. Each version is scanned for prompt injection, data exfiltration, command injection, hardcoded secrets and obfuscated code, including by Cisco's Skill Scanner. Approval is tied to the exact content that was reviewed, so it doesn't carry over silently when a skill changes. A passing check is evidence, not a guarantee.Trim. It shortens noisy test, git and build output before your agent reads it. The full output stays one command away, and your sessions last longer.It syncs across Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. Trim currently covers more than that, but session insights are deepest on Claude Code.There's a permanent free plan for the library, sync, updates and Trust. Trim and AI features are on Individual, with a 7-day trial.I'd love to hear how your skills are scattered today, and what would make you trust a skill you didn't write. I'm here all day and will reply to everything.

today.name: Relay
today.tagline: DocSend for AI agents: send and receive docs with context
today.description: You send a deck or doc. They ask their AI to read it. The AI sees what's on the page, but not the thinking behind it: why you made those choices, what you left out, or what's still open. Relay shares that context with your document, so they and their AI can understand it and ask questions. You choose what to share. Decisions that need your input, like a discount or a date, come back to you. Try a sample relay. No sign-up needed.

today.name: Muse Ember by Meta
today.tagline: Meta's low-cost AI model for high-volume agent tasks
today.description: Muse Ember is Meta's smallest multimodal reasoning model, built to handle the repetitive work behind AI agents. From tool calls and coding subtasks to document extraction and routing, Ember delivers efficient execution at scale. It supports text, images, audio, and video, with a 1M-token context window and pricing starting at $0.10 per million input tokens. Pair it with larger models for planning, and let Ember handle the volume. Available through Meta Model API and Muse Code.

comments.text: Meta just released Muse Ember, its smallest and cheapest Muse model yet.What's interesting is that it's designed specifically for the work AI agents repeat all day: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, document processing, and so on.The idea is to let a larger model handle the difficult planning, then use Ember to execute the smaller tasks at scale.It supports text, images, audio, and video, has a 1M-token context window, and starts at just $0.10 per million input tokens.Pretty interesting option for anyone building agents where inference costs add up quickly.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! I’m Tom, co-founder of Seldon. yesterday.name: Latch.ai

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt! I’m Stefan, co-founder and CEO of Latch.AI has come with a lot of big promises, and yet many of us still spend hours pointing and clicking: pulling reports, moving data between systems, checking one number against another. I started Latch to capture the nuance and free people to focus on the work that really matters.You show Latch how the work gets done, and it helps you see which parts are truly repeatable and where the gray areas are. The goal is to hand the tedium to a machine, so people can spend their time on the judgment calls and new ideas that move things forward.We started with accounting teams, because few processes have more nuance than the month-end close. The capture tool is where the magic happens. As you work, it records three streams: your narration, your screen, and your clicks and keystrokes. That’s how you get a working sidekick without ever writing a prompt or opening a coding agent.Try our free plan today. No credit card required.One question for you: if you had one recurring task you could hand over that would be done right, how impactful would it be for you?

It learns your business during onboarding and comes up with your first week of work on its own.How it works:1️⃣ Answer three questions about your business2️⃣ Empacer drafts your first week: Instagram posts, document drafts, and more3️⃣ You review, edit, approve, and connect your toolsWhat you get:🔌 Integrations. 1000+ tools for your business🧠 Memory. A business profile that remembers everything you’ve said✍️ Marketing content. Posts drafted around what makes your business worth choosing💬 Communication. Customer messages about prices and hours answered in your voiceWhere to find Empacer:🌐 Web. Works right in your browser🤖 Android. The app is already in Google Play🍏 iOS. The app is coming soon🎁 Exclusive for the Product Hunt community: We're offering a 60% off the first subscription period. You can access this discount via this link. 📲 Also, there is a 3-day free trial if you download the app directly from Google Play.We'd love honest feedback on one thing in particular: Voice interfaces have been "the next big thing" for a long time. What’s stopped them from working for you so far?The whole team is here all day: @vehsakam @kenessary @yesmakhan @cool_person_v2

It will even do the appointment setting for you in your own tone and voice.Why bother:Buying windows close fast, usually within days. If nothing is watching, you find out six weeks later, probably from your competitor’s case study.We also pull intent signals most tools skip, like procurement notices, website changes, foot traffic, what's mentioned on a podcast interview, and more. This matters most outside tech, where buyers leave a paper trail but almost never post about what they’re shopping for.Launch offer: 30% off for 3 months using code: PH30FOR3I’ll be hanging out in the comments all day and can't wait to see your questions and use cases!p.s. we do custom signals, too ;) and we have a full white-label, API and MCP.

month.tagline: MCP gateway for production agents that acts on your behalf
month.description: Let your agents use 30,000+ tools across 600+ apps, from Salesforce to GitHub, through one MCP gateway. AgentKit handles auth and integrations, so every action runs as the user who asked, within the scopes they granted. Give each agent only the tools its job needs with Virtual MCP Servers. Add internal APIs as custom connectors. Use Triggers to start an agent the moment an email lands. Built for developers taking agents to production: every call is logged. Free tier: 10,000 tool calls a month.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt,I'm Ravi, co-founder of Scalekit. Today we're launching AgentKit, an MCP gateway that handles auth and tool-calling for AI agents in production.Why now? Over the last year, wiring an agent to a tool got easy. MCP standardized the interface, and any agent can now call Gmail or Salesforce after an afternoon of work.But the tool call is only the surface. Once an agent ships to real users, everything underneath it shows up:whose credentials each call executes withwhich tools each agent should have in contextthe internal systems no catalog coverswhat happens when an upstream API pushes backwho's accountable for every actionThat layer decides whether an agent makes it to production. It's what we built AgentKit for.Try it free: scalekit.com. The free tier includes 10,000 tool calls a month and all 600+ connectors. Make your first tool call from the dashboard, or start from your terminal with npx @ scalekit-inc/cli setup.Here's what it looks like in practice.Say you're shipping a sales agent inside your product. A rep types: "Prep me for the Acme renewal. Pull the deal, the last three email threads, what the team said in Slack, when we last met them, and how much they've used the product this quarter."Four apps, one ask. Getting it working for one rep in a demo is easy. Here's what's underneath when it runs for every rep at every customer:Thousands of OAuth grants, not four. 40 customers × 30 reps × Salesforce, Gmail, Slack and Calendar = 4,800 connected accounts. Each needs its tokens stored, isolated per customer, and refreshed before they expire mid-run. → AgentKit manages connected accounts end to end. Users authorize through an auth link you surface in your app. Tokens live in a per-tenant AES-256 vault, refresh automatically, and are injected at execution time. They never touch your code, logs, or prompts.Every call has to execute as the right user. The agent should see what that rep can see at that customer, and nothing more. Not a shared service account with org-wide access to every inbox. → Every tool call executes with the end user's own credentials, within the scopes they granted.Every tool definition costs context. Gmail alone exposes ~30 tools; four apps put over a hundred on the table. At ~200 tokens per definition, 40 tools burn ~8,000 tokens before the agent does any work, and tool selection gets worse as the list grows. Your prep agent needs about ten tools. Your outbound agent needs a different ten. → Virtual MCP Servers let you compose a tool set per agent role, across connectors. Each role gets one static MCP URL; you mint a short-lived session token per user per run. Smaller context and least-privilege access: ten tool definitions (~2,000 tokens) instead of over a hundred (20,000+).The data you need has no connector. Usage lives in your customer's internal analytics service. No catalog covers it, so you'd build that integration yourself, auth included. → Define it as a custom connector (OAuth 2.0, API key, bearer token, RSA or basic auth), or point AgentKit at a remote MCP server. It runs on the same gateway with the same credential handling and logs as the 600+ built-in connectors.It has to hold up and be auditable. Rate limits, timeouts, upstream errors the model can't act on. Then a deal stage changes and someone asks whether the rep did it or the agent did. → Retries and rate limits are handled on every call. Every call is logged with agent, user, tool and response, and logs stream to Datadog or Splunk.None of this shows up in a demo. All of it shows up in production. AgentKit handles that layer: 30,000+ tools across 600+ apps behind one MCP gateway. And with Triggers, an agent can start on its own the moment an email lands.Python and Node SDKs. Works with the Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs, LangChain, Google ADK, Vercel AI SDK, Mastra, and Claude Code. You keep your framework and backend.Which of these five has slowed your agent down the most?

### مسئله و راه‌حل
اتصال یک ایجنت هوش مصنوعی به ابزارها در مرحله دمو آسان است، اما در محیط پروداکشن (Production) با چالش‌های بزرگی مثل: «اقدامات با دسترسی چه کسی انجام شود؟»، «مدیریت توکن‌های OAuth»، «مصرف بیش از حد توکن‌های پرامپت برای تعریف ابزارها» و «ثبت لاگ و شفافیت» مواجه می‌شویم. Scalekit با ارائه محصول AgentKit یک درگاه MCP مرکزی ایجاد کرده که تمامی فرآیندهای احراز هویت کاربر محور (User-scoped Auth)، بهینه‌سازی بافتار با Virtual MCP و ثبت دقیق logها را مدیریت می‌کند.

### معماری و تکنولوژی
این پلتفرم از استاندارد نوظهور MCP (Model Context Protocol) بهره می‌برد. معماری آن شامل یک گاوصندوق امن (Vault) با رمزنگاری AES-۲۵۶ برای هر مستاجر (Tenant) جهت ذخیره توکن‌ها است. قابلیت Virtual MCP Server باعث می‌شود به جای اضافه کردن صدها تعریف ابزار به بافتار پرامپت، تنها ابزارهای مربوط به نقش کاری کاربر (مثلاً ۱۰ ابزار) بارگذاری شوند که هزینه‌ها را به شدت کاهش داده و دقت مدل را بالا می‌برد. همچنین پشتیبانی از فریم‌ورک‌های متداول مثل LangChain، Vercel AI SDK و SDKهای پایتون/نود پایداری بالایی ایجاد کرده است.

### مدل درآمدی
مدل درآمدی فریم‌یم (Freemium) بر پایه میزان مصرف است. ۱۰,۰۰۰ فراخوانی رایگان در ماه برای جذب توسعه‌دهندگان ارائه شده و برای حجم‌های بالاتر و قابلیت‌های پیشرفته امنیتی و انترپرایز، هزینه دریافت می‌شود.

### نقاط قوت
۱. حل چالش واقعی پروداکشن (احراز هویت و دسترسی کاربر محور به جای دسترسی کلی Admin).
۲. مدیریت بهینه Context Window از طریق سرورهای مجازی MCP.
۳. لاگ‌گیری دقیق و قابلیت ارسال استریم به ابزارهای مانیتورینگ مانند Datadog.

### نقاط ضعف
۱. چالش‌های فنی مربوط به ایجنت‌های زمان‌بندی‌شده (Triggers) هنگامی که کاربر از سازمان خارج می‌شود یا دسترسی‌اش لغو می‌گردد.
۲. وابستگی شدید پلتفرم به پایداری APIهای طرف سوم (Upstream APIs).

### نکته طلایی برای ایران
در بازار ایران، سازمان‌ها به شدت از نشت داده‌ها به هوش مصنوعی می‌ترسند. ساخت یک **MCP Gateway بومی** که دارای کانکتورهای پیش‌فرض به نرم‌افزارهای ایرانی (مثل سیستم‌های مالی سپیدار/همکاران سیستم، CRM دیدار، اتوماسیون چارگون و پیام‌رسان‌های داخلی) باشد و توانایی نصب در زیرساخت داخلی (On-Premise) سازمان‌ها را داشته باشد، یک فرست طلایی و سودآور برای ورود به بازار هوش مصنوعی سازمانی در ایران است.

Full disclosure — I'm a big fan of Anthropic and actually built an app that works exclusively with Claude Desktop for secure local file search. So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.

Identify your triggers, reverse the damage in minutes, and watch the stress curve drop in real time as you act. No 30-minute meditations. No diet overhaul. No long hours at the gym. Just well-timed actions based on YOUR body's data.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! I'm Jane, co-founder of Welltory. Today we're launching Real-Time Stress Relief – a feature that's been years in the making.Why we built this:Most wearables tell you stress was high yesterday. Great. Now what?We spent years analyzing data from 16M+ users to understand something nobody else was looking at: the invisible moments when your heart races while you're sitting still. These "sedentary stress" episodes don't just drain your energy - they're accumulating cardiovascular risk over time.What makes this different:This isn't generic wellness advice. Every insight is based on YOUR personal data and powered by AI trained on millions of people. The app shows you exactly when stress is building right now, what's triggering it, and gives you timed actions to reverse it before you're toast at 8pm.Often it's just: Move for 5 minutes. Simple. Measurable. Effective.Our mission:Preventive health through real-time stress management. This launch is just the beginning - we're working on helping people catch cardiovascular risks before they become problems.My personal lifehack? Just laying down with laptop on a couch during Zoom meetings where I'm not the leading speaker. Sounds lazy, but it works and allows me to be alive for the next and more demanding one.We're done waiting for burnout to tell us we've pushed too far. The data to prevent it is already tracking you – we're just making it impossible to ignore.🎁 Special for the Product Hunt Community:As a thank you, use the promo code welltory_ph_25 to get up to 52% off your annual or lifetime subscription. We'd love for you to experience the full power of one app for your health.Try it and let me know what patterns you discover about yourself. I'd especially love your feedback if you're someone who feels drained by 8pm and can't figure out why.Excited to hear what works for you!Jane

year.name: Gemini 3
year.tagline: Bring any idea to life with multimodal capabilities
year.description: Our most intelligent model that helps you bring any idea to life.

comments.text: Hey Hunters, I am excited to hunt 🚀Google just dropped Gemini 3, and it’s looking seriously powerful — especially for multimodal understanding and agentic tasks. The new “vibe coding” capabilities + faster context grasping make it feel much more intuitive with fewer prompts.You can already try Gemini 3 Pro in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search. Developers can jump in via Google AI Studio and Vertex AI.If you’re building or experimenting with AI workflows, this upgrade is definitely worth checking out. Let me know what you think!

Gemini closing the gap with GPT and Claude is great for the ecosystem. three-way competition drives all of them to ship faster and price more aggressively.the long context window is still Geminis strongest differentiator. when you need to process a 200-page document or a full codebase in one pass, nothing else comes close.for builders integrating AI: the model landscape is moving so fast that locking into any single provider is a risk. multi-model support isnt a nice-to-have anymore. its a necessity.
I used it to analyze ads data and the results were a big leap. It understood the company context and the data, and gave recommendations specific to each ad. Love it and want to keep playing with it.

This is faster and better. Just finished comparing Gemini 3.0 to my usual model. It’s faster and more helpful in brainstorming, but it struggles with precise instructions and multi-step logic. Good for creative tasks, less so for exact ones.

year.name: Framer 3.0
year.tagline: With Agents, Branching, Community, and an all-new design
year.description: Agents bring AI to the canvas to help you design, write, analyze, and organize your sites. We’re also launching Branching, a new way for teams to explore ideas before they go live, and unveiling the new Framer Community, where creators can share and earn. Together, these launches change how teams create, maintain, and scale websites. We think you’ll love it.
year.category: Design Tools • Website Builder • Artificial Intelligence
year.categoryFa: ابزار طراحی • Website Builder • هوش مصنوعی

comments.text: Hey everyone, we’re shipping three huge Framer updates today. 1. Use Agents on the canvas to design, write, analyze, and organize your site. Including ways to connect your own AI’s like Claude Code or Codex to Framer. 2. Branching gives your team a safer way to try ideas before you publish. 3. The new Framer Community gives creators a place to share work and earn from it. Try them out and tell us what you think!

Branching is the part that interests me most. When an agent explores a variation in a branch, can you merge just part of that branch back into the main site, or is it all-or-nothing? And does a branch keep CMS content and interactions intact while you're experimenting?

Really like that Agents can connect to external AI tools like Claude Code rather than being locked into one black-box assistant. How do you handle it when an agent's suggestion conflicts with an existing design system or component constraints — does it flag the conflict or override it?

Really like the direction here — publishing straight from AI-generated design closes a gap a lot of tools leave open. One thing I'd be curious about: as AI-generated content (design or video) becomes the norm, are you thinking at all about provenance/attribution for what's AI-made vs. human-edited? It's something we've had to build for from day one on the video side, and I imagine it'll matter increasingly for design too.
Easy to use, easily customisable. Clients love it.
Branching for design files is the unsung hero here, didn’t know I needed it until now.

The Claude Code / Codex connection is the part I’d want to test first. One question: when an agent changes a live-ish site, does Branching keep the AI edits easy to review as a clean diff, or is it more like comparing page states visually?

The agent/workflow angle in Framer AI Agents is interesting. One thing I’d love to understand is how you handle handoff when the automation is not confident — do users get a clear review step before changes go live?

year.name: Upstream
year.tagline: The inbox designed for humans and agents
year.description: Finally, an inbox you'll look forward to. Agents sort your messages, draft your replies, and clear the grunt work behind the scenes, all in a client so well-crafted that email feels light, fast, fun.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! 👋 Louis here, co-founder of Upstream.When I was at Algolia, I was drowning in 200 emails a day. I was never sure where to focus, and getting through my inbox took forever. I knew it didn’t have to be this way. Instead of creating a new messaging protocol, I bet on rethinking the tool everyone uses: email.We built the first email client where agents do real work alongside people. We designed Upstream to be easy to pick up and fun to use. 📥 Take the noise out of emailAgents automatically triage your inbox, separate signal from noise, and surface only what deserves your attention✍️ Every reply starts with a draftUpstream drafts replies for every conversation that needs one. It also changes your voice based on who you’re talking to and the context of the convo⏰ Never miss a follow-upAgents track open loops and remind you when needed, making sure important conversations don't fall through the cracks🔎 Ask anything about your workAI can instantly find information across your inbox and connected tools: receipts, meeting notes, introductions, decisions, conversations, and more🔗 Bring all your context into your inboxAgents use information from tools like Notion, Calendar, Drive, Granola, and other sources to produce better answers and drafts👉 As a special thank you to the Product Hunt community, you get one free month of Upstream Pro if you sign up at upstream.do and use the code PH26! 👈We are all so excited to hear what you think! Please do reply here and let me know Huge thanks to our hunter @garrytan for hunting us 🙏
congrats team for the success!
